title: Contract observation
description: What one runner observed of one case, one JSON object per line of a runner's output. identity is validated on its own and never compared as a field. A field a runner cannot observe is null, never filled in: rust-host has no stage, exception class or host section, and python-old and python-ref have no core section. No message text is recorded.

outcome.description: Where the public call ended. For rust-host, which makes no public call, the outcome is the core's answer as the route maps it: an accepted query, a description or a materialized request is a success, a refused query INVALID_REQUEST, and a core error a refusal with its code.

host.description: Python runners only: warning classes in the order shown, for information.

origins.description: Each warning in order, its class and the top-level module whose files raised it (null when none of those loaded holds the file): python-core and python-old from T1.29 (register HOST-5), never python-ref.

driver.description: The statements a case ran on DuckDB and DuckDB's own query log, read after the case. On a Python runner, the test-only driver capture (design, Driver capture; decision Q2), null when the run handed the source the driver connection itself (the conservation control); on rust-host (from T1.11e), its DuckDB provider's own record of what it ran, for a case whose core operations read data, and no driver section for a case whose operations read none. Setup, everything run before the connection reaches Schema.from_source (on rust-host, before describe_source starts), is in neither.

statements.description: Each statement the driver ran, in order: the handle it ran on (0 the connection the source was given, then each derived cursor in the order made), the public call it ran in (stage; on rust-host, from_source for describe_source), its SQL text, its typed parameters, every result read from it, its terminal error class, and failed fetch attempts retained separately when an admitted fallback succeeds.

fetch_errors.description: Failed fetch attempts in order, retained when a supported row fallback later completes the same execution; error above is the terminal statement status.

purpose.description: The actual core fetch purpose: source location, result representation metadata or completed native source rows.

bindings.description: Each relation the provider bound by name, with its Arrow contents: DuckDB's register on a Python runner; on rust-host the temporary table it creates from the key set, with the statement it ran to create it (sql), which DuckDB logs as a statement.

incomplete.description: What the capture could not record; any entry fails the capture's checks.

passed_through.description: Attributes read from the driver that the capture neither records nor needs to.

query_log.description: How many QueryLog entries DuckDB wrote after setup: statements (with text) and relations bound (on a Python runner through the API, logged without text; on rust-host the statements creating its temporary tables). Their text is not kept: DuckDB rewrites some statements (a PRAGMA as its table function), and binding names are execution-scoped. On SQLite and Postgres (T2.1a), the driver's own statement log: every statement its cursors executed, and every relation bound by name (ADBC's adbc_ingest), counted alike.

compared.description: How many captured statements' text was compared with the text DuckDB logged for it: all but a PRAGMA, which DuckDB logs as its table function; 0 without the capture.

differing.description: The positions of compared statements whose logged text differs from the captured one.

public.description: Python runners only: the public projection the capture must not change (design, Driver capture): the public Schema, each request the scripted endpoint received, and the public result through to_pandas(). Warnings and the error outcome are host.warnings and outcome.

result_text.description: The SHA-256 of the public result's rows with each value as its text, in order (T3.2, P2-T2.21-1), beside the result so every projection of result is as before: what a more_exact excuse of result.digest, which hashes each value's type, still holds equal; absent on a line recorded before it.

parsed.description: The body as JSON, every number as {"number": its text}; null when it is not JSON.

text_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the rows with each value as its text (str), in order (T3.2, P2-T2.21-1): what a more_exact excuse of digest, which hashes each value's type, still holds equal; absent on a line recorded before it.

core.description: python-core and rust-host only: the inputs each core operation was started with, every fetch the core asked for (its request and the plan its data layer made, in order: the step trace), and its answers: validate_query's acceptance, describe_source's description, materialize's request state, predict's call and result, or the core error's kind and code.

indices.description: One Arrow column, each value a contract scalar.

oneOf.description: predict's start: the model, and the request state the host handed back, its payload with each number as {"number": text}. The request id the host drew is recorded where it reaches the endpoint, in predicted.body's metadata.request_id, which the host checks is the one it started with.

predictions.description: Actual gathered Python prediction invocations, their independently observed native Runs/calls/results and exact presentation relationships; never synthetic Predict operations or public-result reconstruction.

materialization_preparations.description: Actual materialization preparation Runs in start order, their JSON boundaries and lifecycle events. This raw journal supplies no common materialize role or opaque-resource identity claim.

materialization_entries.description: Actual native SQL gather invocations and selected terminal Run or public/Core failure associations; completeness requires the referenced raw journal and actual later state takes.

materialization_guards.description: Actual prepare_frames failure assessment/report Runs scoped to a materialization entry, never invented provider replies.

materialization_capture_capabilities.description: Availability of the installed cancellation interceptor, independent of native failure classification or logical projection.

described.description: describe_source's SourceDescription, as the JSON the core attached.

materialized.description: materialize's RequestState: its version, the query as the core wrote it back, and the payload as the JSON the core attached, each number as {"number": text}, the text the core wrote.

predicted.description: predict's answer: the model call's body as the core wrote it, each number as {"number": text}; the model and call id the endpoint named and its metadata; and the result, its columns and its rows in the endpoint's order, each cell {"i64": digits}, {"f64_bits": the float's IEEE-754 bits as 16 hex digits} or {"utf8": text}.

calls.description: Where predict made more than one call (a forecast's steps, a request asked in several calls), every call's body in the order sent, body the last's (T2.1g); absent for one call.

explanation.description: The result's explanation where the core gave one: its Arrow schema's metadata key explanation, the JSON text the core wrote, as text (T2.13; recorded by both core runners from T2.16a, so the gate holds the hosts to the same bytes); absent where it gave none. An item's explanation and metadata are the result's own columns, among the rows.

capture_capabilities.description: Existing capture interception availability, independent of SDK model policy. Sparse Trace producers never fabricate unavailable products.

legacy_predictions.description: Run-local legacy prediction completion and actually taken products, in actual native Run order. No product is inherited from a predecessor.

model_calls.description: Actually taken legacy Predict CallModel bodies in call order, including failed calls. Absent in older observations means unobserved, not observed-empty. Gathered entry call records remain in predictions.

answered.description: The carried partial Arrow product actually taken from a legacy native error. Null means observed without a carried product; absent means not observed by that checkpoint.

edits.description: From T1.24b, beside inputs, whose shape a gate's checkpoint fixes: each edit_schema's start (the description the core last answered, the schema as the host holds it, the edit) and materialize's held schema, in order; from T3.16 each edit_schema's start is the schema as the host holds it, as plain data, and the edit, and materialize's schema is its input's. A runner of an earlier checkpoint records none.

legacyPredictionResult.description: The actual native completion, with each attachment product present only when the host actually took it.

calls.description: Where predict made more than one call (a forecast's steps, a request asked in several calls), every call's body in the order sent, body the last's (T2.1g); absent for one call.

materializationBytesObservation.description: One actually received JSON bytes attachment; parsed data remains raw and is not reclassified as a domain product by this wrapper.

modelReplyObservation.description: A host-reported reply submitted to the native Run, before forwarding. Null is an actually unobserved reply, distinct from absent historical evidence; it is not physical endpoint delivery proof.

carried.description: Successful SDK carry operation associated by terminal identity/explicit cause with this complete native result Run. This is not a readback of arbitrary public error.details.

key.description: The case a line is of, and the database or warehouse leg it ran on (design choice 2, T2.0f; Phase 3 design choice 1): a DuckDB line is keyed by the bare case ID (case.schema.json's id), a SQLite or Postgres line by <case>@sqlite or <case>@postgres, and a warehouse leg's by <case>@<leg> (databricks-sql, databricks-spark, snowflake, lakebase). Observations, reference lines, captures and baselines use the same keys.

typed.description: A value the capture recorded, as its Python type and repr: the capture's own text, never compared as a value.

parameter.description: A statement's parameter: typed, with its name when the statement binds parameters by name.

result.description: One read of a statement's result: the method, the rows it gave, their Arrow schema when it gave Arrow, their digest as the Python capture computes it (batch boundaries left out; integrity within one runner only, never compared across runners, and rust-host writes none), and their values in the canonical form both languages write (values; decision H9, which the comparator compares).

values.description: A result's columns and rows in canonical form (run_python.py's result_values, sdm-testkit's values, both held to contract/result-vectors.json): the column names, DuckDB's type names where a Python driver gives them (null otherwise), the SHA-256 of the rows in the order read and of the rows sorted by their canonical text, and the kinds of any value the canonical form does not hold.

runner.description: The runner: the reference, the candidate on the core or its old route, the pure-Rust host, or the Java host (Phase 3 design choice 10, T3.11's contract/runners/run_java.py).

cell.description: The runtime cell (design, Runtime cells) whose versions the runner's environment has exactly, or null when it has none's.

commit.description: The checkout the runner ran from.

reference.description: python-ref only: the reference checkout, its environment's hash and the guard's result before the first case and after the last.

native.description: python-core only: the SHA-256 of the sdm_client._native extension module it ran.

native_loaded.description: Python runners: whether sdm_client._native was in sys.modules after the case; null for rust-host.

operations.description: The actual HostRun operations the case started, in order. An observed gathered prediction entry is recorded separately and never adds a synthetic operation.

contract.description: The contract version of the core it ran, or null.

versions.description: The versions the runner ran with: DuckDB's, required of every runner but Java's, whose S0 leg opens no database; Java's host names its runtime's (java), and DuckDB's where its leg opens DuckDB (T3.2).

inputs.description: SHA-256 of the case file's bytes, and of contract/bases.yaml when the runner read it.
